questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could study courses that were relevant for my education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The trip was much more cumbersome and troublesome than expected.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay I guess, not the easiest but I managed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Didn't get any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I got a small apartment. It was fine but I didn't have any options.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed in a new building where we were promised wifi and laundry, but we got none of it. I think there were a lot of good places, but I wouldn't recommend the place where a stayed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a nightmare. You had to try to make it work yourself, while also getting it approved by the host university and your home university. There wasn't really anyone to help at the host university, and there were constant changes to it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was one person at the school who was kind enough to help. But otherwise, it was difficult to find anyone who could assist.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Because there were problems with my home university not being able to approve my courses in time, I didn't get all the subjects I would have liked to have taken.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to reach out to them. I had to write to get the course catalog for the semester I was going abroad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many courses that were not available in English, and there was a lot of overlap, which couldn't work because they placed a high emphasis on attendance.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same (at least for the economic classes)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at the host university was very reminiscent of primary school in Denmark. That is, very different from UCHP; we used paper and pencil for exams. And the teachers weren't super helpful if you asked for extra materials or wanted to discuss exams or assignments in general.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Probabilities, International Economics, Game Theory, European Integration, Intertemporal risk and uncertainty.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Ecotopia courses were more exchange-friendly.

questions.answer: Go to Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn to say the most basic things in French because very few people speak English.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly that very few people speak English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Croissants, coffee, and Paris.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the language if you can't speak French
